column1:
The FOMC statement stays constructive on growth and employment and notes modest further progress on inflation while keeping rates steady and emphasizing data dependence. Beige Book reports across Districts temper that optimism: contacts noted easing labor market conditions and softer hiring expectations, wage growth moderating toward pre‑pandemic norms, more consumer pushback on further price increases with generally more modest price gains, and tight credit conditions alongside ongoing CRE caution. Combined with SLOOS evidence of tighter standards and weaker demand across C&I, consumer, and CRE loans, the backdrop for households and businesses looks more constrained than the statement alone suggests. Netting resilient current activity against moderating wages/prices and tighter bank lending, the tone shifts from moderately positive to cautiously positive.
